evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies Applied Fuzz and Treble Booster as the common production platform behind multiple OEM labels; surviving pot dates cluster 1966-1968, while documented St. Louis Music Supply advertisements establish an early-1968 public sales window. Exact first-production date remains open.

Effects Database identifies the Crown Fuzz and Treble Booster as an early Applied Audio version and lists Goya, Giulietti, Sano and Lou Rose marketed states. Crown remains a label identity rather than a builder record.
Tone Machines documents Lou Rose Music Center distribution in Edison, New Jersey, including a September 1968 opening-weekend offering; the unit belongs to the Applied Fuzz and Treble Booster family.
Effects Database identifies Goya as one of the labels used for early Applied fuzz and treble booster production; exact Goya model-period mapping remains separately cataloged.

Tone Machines identifies the Kadent Treblefuzz as clearly from the same builder as the Applied fuzz platform but notes meaningful construction and circuit differences that may indicate an earlier build. It is retained as a candidate, not a confirmed exact predecessor.

Effects Database records the Applied Rogue as a U.S.-made wedge-style fuzz and notes consistent construction across Applied, Kadent and Nomad branding. Its relationship to the Hohner MF-50 enclosure remains a shared-form candidate rather than proof of identical manufacture.
Effects Database places Kadent Rogue Fuzz within the same Applied Rogue family. Retained as an OEM marketed state pending more model-specific primary documentation.
Effects Database places Nomad Rogue Fuzz within the same Applied Rogue family. Retained separately from the Applied builder record.
Guild partnered with Applied Audio for the FW-3; Effects Database documents the Guild version as Applied-built and identifies multiple other marketed states in the same family.
Effects Database identifies the V-Jay FW-3 as U.S.-made by Applied Audio and lists Guild, Crown, Kadent, Jax-USA, Atlantic, Lou Rose, Magnum and Nomad as related labels.
